Liebe Leser,

leider ist das Führen von Kriegen nicht nur auf die Menschheit begrenzt, *systematische* gewalttätige Auseinandersetzungen (also nicht nur der Kampf zwischen 2 Individuen, wie er ständig passiert) gibt es auch im Tierreich (z.B. bekannt bei Menschenaffen, Ameisen, Zebramangusten, Löwen und Wölfen). Organisierte Gewalt ist uns offenbar in die genetische Wiege gelegt.
Die größte bekannte Schimpansengruppe der Welt hat sich in zwei verfeindete Fraktionen gespalten und führt nun einen tödlichen Konflikt, laut einer kürzlich im *Science* veröffentlichten langjährigen [Studie](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.adz4944). Was ist passiert?

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/stayooutoftherz/23vsEDm4gQuQwARBe5VvX7k7M3czuyXiLZA5G3noZuLosCdZYaknNPGW5wMFkF4D2p5m6.png)

In Ugandas Kibale-Nationalpark lebte bis 2015 die mit etwa 200 Tieren größte bekannte Schimpansengemeinschaft (Ngogo). Über Jahrzehnte hinweg bildeten die Tiere zwei eng verbundene Cluster („Central“ und „Western“), die gemeinsam das Gebiet nutzten, sich mischten und untereinander paarten.
Ab Juni 2015 kam es plötzlich zu Spannungen: Eine Western-Gruppe floh vor einer Central-Gruppe und wurde verfolgt – ein bis dahin noch nie beobachtetes Verhalten. In den folgenden Jahren trennten sich die beiden Fraktionen räumlich und sozial komplett. Sie patrouillierten durch die jeweils eigene Territorien und behandelten die ehemaligen Gruppenmitglieder als Feinde.
Zwischen 2018 und 2024 beobachteten Forscher, wie Western-Schimpansen mindestens sieben erwachsene Männchen und 17 Jungtiere der Central-Gruppe töteten. Weitere 14 Central-Männchen verschwanden spurlos und wurden vermutlich ebenfalls Opfer von Angriffen. Zusätzliche Attacken wurden auch danach dokumentiert.
Laut den Wissenschaftlern führte der extreme Größenzuwachs der Gruppe zu starkem Konkurrenzdruck um Nahrung und Fortpflanzung. Hinzu kamen Wechsel bei den Alphamännchen und der Tod wichtiger „Brücken-Tiere“, die die beiden Cluster früher verbanden. Das soziale Gefüge brach auseinander. 

Ein ähnlicher Fall ereignete sich in den 1970er-Jahren im Gombe-Nationalpark (Tansania) und wurde von Jane Goodall beobachtet. Damals zweifelten einige Forscher an der Natürlichkeit des Konflikts, weil die Tiere an menschliche Futterstellen gewöhnt waren. Die Ngogo-Beobachtung gilt nun als erster eindeutiger Beleg für einen "natürlichen" Bürgerkrieg bei Schimpansen.

Der Erstautor Aaron Sandel (University of Texas) sieht darin eine Parallele zum Menschen: Konflikte entstehen oft nicht primär durch kulturelle Unterschiede, sondern durch den Zerfall persönlicher sozialer Beziehungen. Friedensförderung sollte deshalb vor allem auf den Erhalt und die Pflege zwischenmenschlicher Kontakte setzen – auch über Konfliktgrenzen hinweg. Ich bezweifle das aber, denn Krieg entsteht öfter durch individuelle Führungspersönlichkeiten und deren Machtanspruch, die die Folgen des Krieges meist selbst nicht zu tragen haben und weniger durch persönliche Feindschaften.

Wie seht Ihr das?

Hi, guys!

I have a lot of photoshoots planned today, but first I have to go to the post office to pick up and mail packages, and also wrap gifts for my husband's birthday, which is almost a month away, but I like to have everything ready in advance. I already have three gifts ready, and I want everything to be perfect this year, so I'm planning on wrapping them in beautiful paper so he can unwrap them and fully experience the joy.

I also need to send books to a friend, so that's another little surprise.

Yesterday I joined a group of illustrators I don't know; we're planning to meet for coffee and drawing. I don't know any of them, and this will be my first time doing something like this, but I hope everything goes well. I'm really looking forward to it. I've got a lot going on this month, and I don't know if it's too much for just me. But I think I'll manage somehow.

I'm pretty far behind on filming right now, so I need to catch up. I haven't filmed any pranks in a while, and that needs to be done, too, but I can't find the time. And I can't find the right mood either. But I need to find it and do it.

So, I actually have a lot of plans. I need to get myself together, pull myself together, and process them all one by one, because the longer I put them off, the more they pile up, and there's nowhere left to put them, and there's already too many.

So now I'm finishing my coffee, quickly running to the post office, then getting myself together and filming videos until I can't stand it. And tomorrow I need to get back to walking the dogs, because I've had almost a week without any exercise.

Have a great day, everyone!

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWNqkBjyFeq1DSuaC4WrcEvWwST3JXhYyam1xPZdUudC9/1775801532662.jpg)


> "Wars are never won. Victory is achieving your goal. And she had achieved it." 

So we begin the review of one of the latest books I read, Limbo by Mazzucco. This is a powerful book about war, redemption, post-traumatic stress disorder, the condition of women, family, and ideals. A book that truly encompasses many themes and food for thought. Let me tell you about the plot: it begins in Ladispoli, a simple town in Lazio, home to simple people. Manuela Paris, one of the rare female marshals seriously injured and miraculously alive in an attack in Afghanistan, returns here, captivated by the glory and exaltation of her fellow citizens. Manuela returns home and wants only to face her inner demons in silence, but the citizens and her family wrap themselves around her like a noose. Manuela hasn't been the same since she returned. Coming close to death, losing colleagues and friends has thrown her into a crisis. Every loud noise, everything reminds her of her missions, and so she shuts herself away at home, in her own world, in the company of her somewhat unruly family, especially her lively, promiscuous sister, always seeking excitement. And then there's a silent companion who calms her down: the man smoking on the terrace of the hotel across the street, a constant presence that becomes almost mystical for Manuela, locked in her grief and intent on battling post-traumatic stress disorder.


💥💥💥💥💥💥💥💥💥💥💥💥💥💥💥💥

«Las guerras nunca se ganan. La victoria consiste en alcanzar la meta. Y ella la había alcanzado». 

Así comenzamos la reseña de uno de los últimos libros que leí: Limbo, de Mazzucco. Se trata de una obra impactante sobre la guerra, la redención, el trastorno de estrés postraumático, la condición de la mujer, la familia y los ideales. Un libro que abarca numerosos temas y que invita a la reflexión. Permítanme contarles la trama: comienza en Ladispoli, un pueblo sencillo del Lacio, hogar de gente sencilla. Manuela Paris, una de las pocas mujeres alguaciles que resultó gravemente herida y sobrevivió milagrosamente a un ataque en Afganistán, regresa a este lugar, cautivada por la gloria y la exaltación de sus conciudadanos. Manuela vuelve a casa deseando enfrentarse a sus demonios internos en silencio, pero los ciudadanos y su familia la acosan como una soga. Manuela no ha vuelto a ser la misma desde su regreso. Haber estado al borde de la muerte y haber perdido compañeros y amigos la ha sumido en una profunda crisis. Todo ruido fuerte, todo le recuerda sus misiones, así que se encierra en casa, en su propio mundo, en compañía de su familia, algo rebelde, especialmente de su hermana, vivaz y promiscua, siempre en busca de emociones fuertes. Y luego está un compañero silencioso que la tranquiliza: el hombre que fuma en la terraza del hotel de enfrente, una presencia constante que se vuelve casi mística para Manuela, sumida en su dolor y empeñada en combatir el trastorno de estrés postraumático.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQ6BeeKejVsgVryArkVDGAtP7x3mwLyNMaPb6AunRK8Ba/1775801556210.jpg)

In this book, Manuela first retraces her life from her rebellious adolescence, the conflicts with her mother and father, the turning point when she discovers and decides that her destiny lies in the military, the beginning of her passion or near obsession for military life, perhaps idealized but so longed for, from a rebellious and unscrupulous teenager to a woman who desires rigor and discipline, the difficulties she encounters as a woman in the army, the tough training, the hazing, the sexism, life with her comrades, the climb to the role of marshal made up of many falls and failures, doubts, fears and sacrifices but also of the iron will to succeed at all costs. And while she retraces the past, there is also the present: she will meet the man smoking at the window, a strange guy who somehow manages to penetrate Manuela's armor and bring her some of the lightheartedness she needs after all the bad things she saw on the mission, but he will also bring doubts and conflicting feelings.

💥💥💥💥💥💥💥💥💥💥💥💥💥💥💥

En este libro, Manuela reconstruye su vida desde su adolescencia rebelde, los conflictos con sus padres, el punto de inflexión en el que descubre y decide que su destino está en el ejército, el comienzo de su pasión, o casi obsesión, por la vida militar, quizás idealizada pero anhelada, de una adolescente rebelde y sin escrúpulos a una mujer que desea rigor y disciplina, las dificultades que encuentra como mujer en el ejército, el duro entrenamiento, las novatadas, el sexismo, la vida con sus camaradas, el ascenso al puesto de mariscal, plagado de caídas y fracasos, dudas, miedos y sacrificios, pero también de una férrea voluntad de triunfar a toda costa. Y mientras reconstruye el pasado, también está el presente: conocerá al hombre que fuma en la ventana, un tipo extraño que de alguna manera logra penetrar la coraza de Manuela y brindarle algo de la ligereza que necesita después de todas las cosas malas que vio en la misión, pero también le traerá dudas y sentimientos contradictorios.



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRRjBKadmk7sfKgXDTZUxpFfgeWPJHwuZgsj8Cq4WrNe7/1775801556352.jpg)

And then there's the part about the memories of the missions, from her first mission abroad, about how hard it was to be assigned to Afghanistan and about Afghanistan, a land of conflict but also of beauty, about how she found herself in this new world made up of a land so different from Italy and Lazio, about the emotional disorientation, about the belief that she was useful, that she could bring peace with guns in hand. Of that place that in the book almost seems like a disturbing dream, with its welcoming, hostile, or dangerous people, its faces marked by constant wars and pain. And Manuela reflects on how much all this cost her and whether it was worth it, reflects on her blind military faith and on what she did or didn't do in Afghanistan, and at the same time tries to heal her body and mind and get used to normal life again. It's a book I recommend because, in addition to being well-written, it truly addresses many themes in depth and is a book that has a certain strength but also a sensitivity. In short, for me, Mazzucco confirms herself as one of the finest Italian writers.

💥💥💥💥💥💥💥💥💥💥💥💥💥💥💥💥

Y luego está la parte sobre los recuerdos de las misiones, desde su primera misión en el extranjero, sobre lo difícil que fue ser destinada a Afganistán y sobre Afganistán, una tierra de conflicto pero también de belleza, sobre cómo se encontró a sí misma en este nuevo mundo formado por una tierra tan diferente de Italia y Lacio, sobre la desorientación emocional, sobre la creencia de que era útil, de que podía traer la paz con las armas en la mano. De ese lugar que en el libro casi parece un sueño perturbador, con su gente acogedora, hostil o peligrosa, sus rostros marcados por guerras y dolor constantes. Y Manuela reflexiona sobre cuánto le costó todo esto y si valió la pena, reflexiona sobre su fe militar ciega y sobre lo que hizo o dejó de hacer en Afganistán, y al mismo tiempo intenta sanar su cuerpo y su mente y acostumbrarse de nuevo a la vida normal. Es un libro que recomiendo porque, además de estar bien escrito, realmente aborda muchos temas en profundidad y es un libro que tiene cierta fuerza pero también sensibilidad. En resumen, para mí, Mazzucco se confirma como una de las mejores escritoras italianas.

#### In the world of Bitcoin, **you are the boss of your own bank.** To keep your treasure safe, you use something called a **Private Key**.

#

### The Secret Code 🤫
A Private Key isn't a small metal key like the one for your front door. It’s a super-long, super-secret string of numbers and letters. Think of it as a **Magical Digital Fingerprint**. 

* **Your Public Address:** This is like your mailbox. Anyone can see it and drop a Bitcoin "letter" inside.
* **Your Private Key:** This is the only thing that can open the mailbox. 



### The Golden Rule: Your Key, Your Treasure 🏆
Because this key is your "Secret Signature," it gives you all the power. 
1.  **If you have the key:** You can move your Bitcoin anywhere in the world instantly.
2.  **If someone else gets your key:** They can take your Bitcoin! It’s like giving someone the combination to your diary—or your piggy bank.
3.  **If you LOSE your key:** This is the most important part. If the key is gone, the Bitcoin stays locked in its digital chest **forever**. Even the smartest computer in the world can't open it without that magical fingerprint.

### 🔍 Pro-Tip: The "Seed Phrase"
Since long strings of numbers are hard to remember, most people use a **Seed Phrase**. This is a list of 12 or 24 simple words (like *apple, mountain, bicycle, sun*). These words are the "map" to your Private Key. 

**Never, ever share these words with anyone!** Not even a "helper" on the internet. If you keep them safe, your money is safe.

---

### 🎮 The "Secret Signature" Challenge
1.  Take a piece of paper and write down a secret "Code Word" (like *SpaceTiger77*). 
2.  This is your **Private Key**. 
3.  Now, try to describe your Code Word to a partner **without saying it**. 
4.  If they can guess it, they "stole" your key! 
5.  If you hide the paper and forget the word, you "lost" your treasure.

**Real Bitcoin pros write their keys down on paper or metal and hide them in a very safe spot!** ---

Who knows if these watches are actually correct or not.  A study I recently read came to the conclusion that **all manufacturers** of sport watches are incorrect with their calculations but I think that it would be unreasonable to expect some little thing on your wrist to give perfectly accurate results when the only way to truly determine such figures is to be hooked up to all sorts of scientific gosmers that measure so many things that your body is doing.

But I have read a lot of literature about how walking burns just as much (from a caloric perspective) as running does, it just takes a lot longer.

On days where I don't really feel like I have it in me to do a bunch of cardio I will still go for a very long walk because of the fact that when I was seriously overweight, I lost a ton of weight by doing very little else other than simply walking because I was so fat that I couldn't really do anything else. 

<center> https://darebee.com/images/guides/walking-jogging-running.jpg
[src](https://darebee.com/images/guides/walking-jogging-running.jpg)</center>

I don't necessarily believe all the things that I read online because these days it seems like no matter what you read someone is trying to tell you to do it differently and they also want to sell you something at the same time.  I know from my own experience in my own life that just walking really will help you to lose weight if that is your objective.   

The type of walking I was doing the other day though, this would be considered extremely relaxed, probably a bit too relaxed. 

<center> 
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/normie.fitness/23tRxWjyDmdTujv2ckSmEg7RHgqj19wAeVBRSRb3GmkYteMJ7r9BwSQoETuR8w7LCxPGB.png)
</center>

330 calories isn't a lot, especially for someone like me that can replace those in about 20 minutes with a couple of beers. It's more than zero though and it's always kind of nice for mental health as well as physical health to get out of the house and be in the closest thing this enormous city has to nature.  

<center>  
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/normie.fitness/23tGTmQYESYmtRYmsKs548LmnrwAXy11Nhc6QcdyRJtuvc3zxUXk3uX6kYmAyfDWciVGj.png)
</center>

The heart rate is kind of a joke honestly, It is rare for me to not break a sweat at all no matter what I am doing, but it's more effort than I would have been putting forth if I was at my desk or sitting on the sofa.  

<center> 
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/normie.fitness/Eo6BEM3TkcuB6dQJT57HfX4dqeoeR8YPcfV4XbgkNMx7a56pTiPF9Aqks4ooJUg6C7e.png)
</center>

At no point in time was I ever pushing it even a little bit and I just alternated between listening to the sounds of the city, which isn't that bad on these walking paths, and also listening to a podcast.  Seriously folks, if you are trying to lose a bit of weight and you already have a show that you like to listen to, why not combine the two?   Lately I have been listening to something like a pub quiz and I always end up learning some things that I didn't know before.  

When I run a 5k, my watch tells me that my caloric burn is a little bit higher than this, but not very much.  

> While calorie counts are useful for tracking long-term trends, they should be interpreted as directional signals rather than precise metrics

What that means to me is that the data your watch gives you at the end of whatever activity you are doing should not be taken literally and are not an accurate measurement of what you are actually doing.  While the algorithyms are actually quite complex and take into account your individual age, weight, height, and history of exercise that it knows, the general consensus is that all sport watches, even the expensive ones, are 25-40% incorrect about what the actual calories burned are.

That's just fine by me but clinical trials with really expensive and accurate (so they say) equipment also has shown that running vs jogging vs walking burns a pretty close amount of calories based on the **distance traveled**.  There would be exceptions of course such as seriously pushing your heart rate close to maximum, but for normal people like you and I, there is too much risk of injury to really try to be doing that on a regular basis.

here is a picture that will never not be funny to me.
<center> 
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/normie.fitness/23t77FUKhLZMxmAV3ni7LG1Jf1ty8gfE3pNT2TVpAWgiBnxNvpU6KFA9j924VJV9uKA7w.png)
</center>

I always get a little chuckle out of my stats after I forgot to wear my watch for like half a day and since the computers don't really know how to determine if it was plugged up or not as far as the watch is concerned I have been siting in one place with no heartbeat at all of hours and hours.

result.body: ![service-pnp-jpd-02100-02199v.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/maxinpower/23x1DAwMATricULiEHuwSiPEBbuoTQtY2LuaBEQeNGGSvEBH38VALSf6ExMRLKqHNowr4.jpg) Today, we're treating ourselves to another ukiyo-e picture. This Japanese art form reached its peak during the Edo period and was best known for its colorful woodblock prints and drawings, which are still very popular today. The Library of Congress has collected a large number of these woodblock prints and made them available in digital form on its [website](https://www.loc.gov/collections/japanese-fine-prints-pre-1915/about-this-collection/). Fortunately, these images are not subject to copyright, so I am able to share them with you from time to time here in this blog. [Today's woodblock print](https://www.loc.gov/resource/jpd.02199/) depicts groups of women enjoying hanami in Ueno Park—one of the most famous places for cherry blossom viewing in the Edo period. The scene dates from the late 1700s and was created by Katsukawa Shunzan, an artist of the early ukiyo-e school. The women wear magnificent kimonos and move through the blossoming cherry trees with a mixture of grace and everydayness. The composition emphasizes not only the beauty of nature, but also the social rituals and fashionable details of the time. Ueno was not only a place of relaxation, but also a reflection of social elegance. And that still applies today, because even now, Ueno Park is one of the most popular destinations during the sakura season. Although I probably have to admit that it must have been a little more peaceful and civilized there during the Edo period. In my opinion, Ueno Park is far too crowded these days and therefore inevitably too noisy and littered with trash to be able to enjoy the cherry blossoms in peace. As always, I wish I had a time machine that could take me back to times long past. The Japanese capital during the Edo period would be surely a place I would love to visit. But until then, let's look at these wonderful old works of art and keep dreaming... ![service-pnp-jpd-02100-02199v.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/maxinpower/23x1DAwMATricULiEHuwSiPEBbuoTQtY2LuaBEQeNGGSvEBH38VALSf6ExMRLKqHNowr4.jpg) DEUTSCH Heute gönnen wir uns mal wieder ein Ukiyo‑e Bild. Diese japanische Kunstform hatte ihren Höhepunkt in der Edo‑Zeit, und war vor allem durch ihre farbigen Holzschnitte und Zeichnungen bekannt, die sich auch heute noch großer Beliebtheit erfreuen. Die **Bücherei des Kongresses der Vereinigten Staaten von Amerika** hat eine große Anzahl dieser Holzschnittdrucke gesammelt und stellt sie auf ihrer [Webseite ](https://www.loc.gov/collections/japanese-fine-prints-pre-1915/about-this-collection/)in digitaler Form zur Verfügung. Und glücklicherweise unterliegen diese Bilder dort keinem Urheberrecht, so dass ich sie euch ab und zu hier in diesem Blog vorstellen darf. [Das heute Holzschnittbild](https://www.loc.gov/resource/jpd.02199/) zeigt Gruppen von Frauen beim Hanami im Ueno-Park – einem der berühmtesten Orte für Kirschblütenschauen im Edo-Zeitalter. Die Szene stammt aus der späten 1700er-Jahre und wurde von Katsukawa Shunzan gestaltet, einem Künstler der frühen Ukiyo-e-Schule. Die Frauen tragen prachtvolle Kimonos und bewegen sich durch die blühenden Kirschbäume mit einer Mischung aus Anmut und Alltag. Die Komposition betont nicht nur die Schönheit der Natur, sondern auch die sozialen Rituale und modischen Details der damaligen Zeit. Ueno war nicht nur ein Ort der Erholung, sondern auch ein Spiegel gesellschaftlicher Eleganz. Und das gilt auch noch für heute, denn auch in diesen Tagen ist der Ueno-Park eines der beliebtesten Ausflugsziele während der Sakura-Saison. Obwohl ich wahrscheinlich zugeben muss, dass es in der Edo-Zeit dort ein wenig geruhsamer und auch gesitteter zugegangen sein muss. Meiner Meinung ist der Ueno-Park heutzutage viel zu überlaufen und daher zwangsläufig viel zu laut und auch vermüllt, als das man sich dort in Ruhe die Kirschblüten ansehen könnte. Wie immer wünschte ich mir auch diesmal eine Zeitmaschine, welche mich in längst vergangene Zeiten bringt. Gerade die japanische Hauptstadt in der Edo-Zeit wäre ein Ort, den ich gerne einmal besuchen würde. Aber nun ja, bis es soweit ist, betrachten wir diesen wundervollen alten Kunstwerke und träumen dabei ein wenig.. ![blog-ende.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/maxinpower/23tv6H18WKn98nBVkn2MwVhwWsuFRFgjBGwxLEMVhRZD7zRRbFokaNiAn39fUaB3TxVX6.png)

@LadiesofHive Community [Contest #283](https://hive.blog/hive-124452/@ladiesofhive/ladies-of-hive-community-contest-283) questions for the week are: 1️⃣ Self Care: We fall sick, we get well because we took care by taking medication, it's human. But we tend to overlook or under care when we are not sick, when we feel strong and healthy. So, here's the reminder question: How do you care for your body and mind when you are not sick? What is your everyday health care routine like? ~ 𝐀𝐍𝐃 / 𝐎𝐑 ~ 2️⃣ Hobby Crush: Most of us have hobbies we spend little or more time doing, but there are hobbies we admire others do. What is that one hobby you wish you could do for fun, too, and why can't you adopt it for your free time?
🌸🌸🌸🌸🌸🌸🌸🌸🌸🌸🌸🌸🌸🌸🌸🌸🌸🌸🌸
That's a fact that a lot of people only care about themselves when they are unwell and the moment, they get well then again, they go back to a absent minded life. Sadly, in my life I have always had sick people around me, and have been taking care of them. They have been my very dear ones so I cannot even shy away from taking care of them, but looking at them I always feel motivated to take care of my self all the time. I do not wish an ailing old age or the one where I am dependent on anyone. I want to be healthy, active and mobile for as long as I live. But it does not happen overnight. It's about how you have taken care of yourself all your life it will give you results in old age. My daily routines of my self-care on my fitness and keeping my muscles strong are doing Yoga, meditation, walking 3k to 5K steps daily. Besides this, I follow a healthy and balanced diet through the week. Over the week I indulge in some junk food but that too with mindfulness. ![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRiLebf5okLHZc9WTs3ByxBzCSkXF12pUcPCNA992Nqo8/image.png) [Source](https://pixabay.com/illustrations/woman-girl-female-posing-pose-9457927/) Twice a year I do a full health check-up and then based on the results, I add up vitamin and mineral supplements into my daily diet. I like to drink alcohol so I have a glass of red wine once a week. It's not that I do not indulge in any unhealthy foods and drinks, I do but keeping everything in control and also ensuring to minimize the impact of it on my health. I spend time in nature and doing things I love and enjoy, all of this keeps me in a positive state of mind. I enjoy travelling so even over the weekends I do short travels even if it is for a day, it makes me feel good mentally and emotionally. Wellness is not a day's job it is a daily job and the most important one. To be practical, every single day it's not possible to follow a healthy routine but it can be balanced out with 1 or 2 cheat days in a week and then following up with some measures that will take care of the junk. Like Friday and Saturday are my cheat days and then Sunday is my fasting day. Balance is important. If I try to be too stringent then it is possible that I will end up doing more wrong things and not taking care of myself. ***Thank you for visiting my blog.*** 👼🏻👼🏻💖💖🌹🌺🌸 ![29074314-2B4D-4B6F-95BF-C36DA204CA63.gif](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVoUR1s5svnvaDKw3hD89uysyEH1eN7xEa6HmvDkZNJ4g/29074314-2B4D-4B6F-95BF-C36DA204CA63.gif) ![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNntqsReJZaxt1UTvYj7JwzBKZP2cdt7C8Ujg437EehKT/image.png) ***

### English _______ # Australia: The Sydney Opera House After a Visit to Milson Park _______ When we think of Australia, we think of an entire continent—and in a way, it almost is one—except that it’s not the only country in Oceania. We think of a rich, distant land where only a few have the chance to live. We think of the English language, the United Kingdom, and I don’t know about you, but I think a lot about Finding Nemo and the famous Sydney Opera House—which is the reason for this post. I won’t talk to you about the historical features of this city landmark because AI has already surpassed Google in that regard, but I will share my experience visiting it from eastern Sydney.
> ### Español ______ > # Australia: La Ópera de Sydney tras una visita a Milson Park _______ > Cuando pensamos en Australia pensamos en todo un continente, y casi casi que lo es, solo que no es el único país de Oceanía. Pensamos en una tierra rica y lejana, a donde unos pocos pueden acceder para vivir allí. Pensamos en el idioma inglés, en Reino Unido y yo no sé ustedes, pero yo pienso bastante en Buscando a Nemo y en la famosa Ópera de Sydney. lo cual es el motivo de este post. > No les hablaré de las características históricas de este emblema de la ciudad porque para eso ya superó a Google la IA, pero les comentaré mi experiencia al visitarla desde el este de Sydney.
________________________ ![IMG_5984.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EqFsQyfytr4obyzmfA7B9uYJJWqYFJDCSoQ5BmNsh77ft4QKWCkty8XGQVa37u9GNBf.jpeg) ![IMG_5950.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EqUdQmYXkprNC9vJV5nEmiNiZei8NWwQGLvDozKebxkhQtvxRzcas3797eP8HQLjmFy.jpeg) ![IMG_6054.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EpXJbNi6nDozAkPehJHXUU5CGc7VzCzjxShWnZyx6kSBpTTqF9ehkHshhqL966uS3LP.jpeg) ![IMG_5952.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EpVBX6itNXLKCESu8fNMpdCVoyMJGo8zWeJ9ouW5Cx6quaHCBocBrrb8ZChrwg2ZoeR.jpeg) _______________
First, I should mention that Australia is so vast that I think it would take a couple of years to explore it all, so I decided to visit just two cities: Sydney and Melbourne. Each of these cities is enormous in its own right, as well as complex and diverse, because the urban areas are already bustling with energy, but they also boast natural sites of global significance. Today I’m taking you to Sydney and its Opera House, from Milson Park and across the Sydney Harbour Bridge. This was the moment when I was jumping for joy inside, because I could see the city’s icon—which for over 10 years had been my dream, my goal, my objective that seemed so far away—and thanks to God, who gave me the courage to take action, I was able to reach it. The reason I stayed only two weeks in Australia and a month in Thailand or India (another dream) was the cost of staying in this country. Since my nearly four-month trip was initially going to be funded mainly by volunteer work—which is also great for any resume—I had booked flights based on those opportunities. But since they wanted to hold onto my passport during my first volunteer stint teaching yoga in Thailand, I decided to cancel the other three trips I had planned in that same country and in Australia, since I thought that if I was about to fulfill my dream, there was no reason to take a risk. Later, I realized that I deserved that trip simply because I wanted it.
> Primero comentar que Australia es tan grande, que recorrerlo yo creo que tomaría un par de años, por lo que yo decidí visitar solamente 2 ciudades: Sydney y Melbourne. Cada una de ellas en sí, también es enorme, además de compleja y variada, porque la zona urbana ya cuenta con suficiente dinamismo, pero además estos puntos tienen sitios naturales de interés mundial. > Hoy les traigo a Sydney y a su Ópera, desde Milson Park y a través del Puente de la Bahía de Sydney. Este fue el momento en que internamente saltaba de felicidad, pues pude ver al ícono de la ciudad que durante más de 10 años había sido mi sueño, mi meta, mi objetivo que parecía tan lejano, y que gracias a Dios que me dio el coraje de moverme, pude alcanzar. > El motivo por el que me quedé únicamente 2 semanas en Australia y un mes en Tailandia o India (otro sueño), fue el valor de la estadía en este país. Dado que inicialmente mi viaje de casi 4 meses estaría principalmente sostenido por voluntariados, había comprado vuelos acordes a estas experiencias, además enriquecedoras para cualquier CV. Pero como quisieron retenerme el pasaporte en el primer voluntariado para dar clases de Yoga en Tailandia, decidí cancelas los otros 3 que tenía en ese mismo país y en australia, ya que pensé que si estaba a punto de cumplir mi sueño, no tenía por qué arriesgarme, y luego entendí que merecía aquel viaje porque sí, porque lo deseaba.
___________ ![IMG_5940.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EoEr2WTbuSXdswpmYtLsCK3crbY3ve4maUaQkdWc9JWw5f9dJ7rwurpwGrff2AApfvP.jpeg) ![IMG_5939.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EoAaJwDWwDsqQ8BB4Zz4Jt2mYGcq4kfbZHzXaRdZk9bzFQEKJcp3LqmpX949qKCYYmT.jpeg) ![IMG_5954.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EqNEGGMBMKpV23dAREEoarHy2kS9cUe4c8unHqtRnCE93tWjVhzMgXkhNCvdK2BwWXe.jpeg) ![IMG_5943.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EpvhP8XtoAQx65Nx7X7kZR6q512rh4xayQS78oaa3WJTdjYwsvDdRDtcE8rbvzru7FX.jpeg) ![IMG_5946.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EnmBjXLEp7nFcG5Q9bLY1xCx2KQytp6SiuWkkz7Mu8JE2kykAdfkPqPynheBDpVVnLL.jpeg) ___________________
Well, Milson Park is one of those less touristy spots, one of those more local places. It’s located north of Sydney, just past the bridge. I took public transportation there from my hostel—a sort of tram or train. The park was empty of people, and I noticed a family enjoying the place. This was also the place where I really started paying attention to the birds—there are so many of them in Sydney, both in the city and in urban areas a bit further from the center. There, I began to see species that were exotic to me, since they were birds I had either never seen before or had only seen as a child at animal theme parks.
> Pues bien, Milson Park es uno de esos sitios no muy turísticos, esos lugares más locales. Se encuentra al norte de Sydney, pasando el puente. Yo fui hasta allí en transporte público desde mi hostel, en una especie de tranvía o tren. > El parque estaba despejado de gente, y me llamó la atención una familia que disfrutaba del sitio. Además este fue el lugar en el que realmente empecé a prestar atención a las aves, que son muchísimas en Sydney, incluso en la ciudad, y en sectores urbanos un poco más alejados del núcleo, se empiezan a ver especies para mi, exóticas, pues se trataba de aves que o nunca había visto o que de pequeña había visto en parques temáticos de animales.
__________ ![IMG_5994.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EoyR23HjzWu2irEESKiD9MmT1wbxXTB6R8HioTn13kfgCo3R6dRDTvNoSPixLEvqHpY.jpeg) ![IMG_5963.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EptayUW7rTRJQW1LvZ4o59GdYkWcCTWPJ1XEkhgkPpPYz8pCFuQrKCvYmJiF2kqvoVi.jpeg) ![IMG_5961.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EprShdxyfPjkexPNkzZbht2ZaHG8ywe7AJSyqb7dLZn5QS7akBXzgEjrrEvvKabnGRK.jpeg) ![IMG_6023.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EpQvNbaid4WjBUQACsnWAH7u4YPLdQErtjovJ44oVPa3riRWDFfKdNcxwEUnnHUKtkG.jpeg) ![IMG_6025.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/241tWigGfuc1FaQwvL1Kf3f37VCuWNKG6qxy79SW3FDCxh2vmbJarLguvdU8PPqLq8zUV.jpeg) _______________
Milson Park is a place to relax, enjoy yourself, and really connect with Sydney. It’s quiet, surrounded by nature, and offers beautiful scenery. Even so, despite the sheer size of downtown Sydney, I have to say it’s not an overly noisy city and is surprisingly spacious. From Milson Park, I walked back across the Harbour Bridge, something that had become a little dream of mine during this trip. And it was a beautiful experience, as there’s a dedicated pedestrian section. From there, I got a panoramic, bird’s-eye view of the Opera House, which filled me with so much emotion that I even started to cry. I was fulfilling a huge dream, something I’d deeply desired, as I watched that structure rise above the water, resembling waves on the sea.
> Milson Park es un espacio para relajarse, disfrutar y para conectar mucho mejor con Sydney. Tiene silencio, mucha naturaleza y unos paisajes preciosos. Igualmente a pesar de la magnitud del núcleo de Sydney, debo decir que no es una ciudad demasiado ruidosa y es sorprendentemente espaciosa. > Desde Milson Park, regresé cruzando el Puente de la Bahía, algo que ya se había convertido en un pequeño sueño dentro de mi viaje. Y fue una experiencia hermosa, pues tiene un sector específico para peatones. > Desde allí, obtuve una vista panorámica y así aérea de la Ópera, lo cual me llenó tanto de emoción que hasta llegué a llorar. Estaba cumpliendo un gran sueño, algo que deseaba profundamente, mientras veía a aquella estructura elevarse sobre el agua y simulando olas en el mar.
________ ![IMG_6057 2.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/Eqb1WusqfLecCksLPMqtHjkE2pfzFwjZosCHZWaxa1ficSn8URuY5Pke4dpZvCssDik.jpeg) ![IMG_5957.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EpLfaEQCh7BuCHGWdYPY59muS5qB1WDnEw9iwpD7JNDz1FVCxZM9uzktgujShCeod2E.jpeg) ![IMG_6019.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EowGfGny98NCs77YXh5p8yG3LPncuZHVZf1f9qq2TGWrrg4Rt5r7FPyp2uQYZpL9SBZ.jpeg) ![IMG_6055.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EnqSeV5rHqXGVEcbXxbv6NBdCZwt2Y2UwAtTYW96nrjJGJfwDkZBp9QUzSz3SFLiwJn.jpeg) ![IMG_6013.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/23tbtmfqj3MaUQBSeJtVdWBBLtkKbXetgUuHE7XZnCQXQGiZh6kqyMHNvkh9g3qawE9w2.jpeg) ________
The Sydney Opera House isn’t just a cultural landmark; it’s a gathering place, a social hub where hundreds of people come every day to have a few beers, grab a bite to eat, and enjoy the Australian day and night. That afternoon, I myself enjoyed an Aperol while watching people come and go, chatting and laughing, and I sat comfortably on one of the stone benches—which are far more comfortable than any regular bench—that are there for those who visit this venue in a more casual or passing manner.
> La Ópera de Sydney no es solamente un sitio cultural, sino que se trata de un lugar de encuentro, un lugar social donde cientos de personas a diario se disponen a tomar unas cervezas, a comer algo, a disfrutar del día y de la noche australiana. > Yo misma aquella tarde disfruté de un Aperol mientras contemplaba a las personas ir y venir, charlar, reír, y cómodamente me senté a un costado en una de las reposeras de piedra pero bastante más cómodas que cualquier banco, que están allí para quienes se acercan a este predio de manera más informal o pasajera.

昨天下午，跟着大部队去江西省图书馆转了一圈。按大区轮流安排，我们是最后一组，时间卡得特别紧，直接定在下午四点，就在图书馆一楼展厅。
 ![QdER4FSFI28zuVxC_IMG_20260409_162201.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/trina77/images/QdER4FSFI28zuVxC_IMG_20260409_162201/QdER4FSFI28zuVxC_IMG_20260409_162201.webp)
这次图书馆之行是领导特意安排，为的是我们这次“书香校园”的建设项目，让我们看看省图书馆是如何做的。
![N2i1Dwno36yZVjAZ_IMG_20260409_160316.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/trina77/images/N2i1Dwno36yZVjAZ_IMG_20260409_160316/N2i1Dwno36yZVjAZ_IMG_20260409_160316.webp)

![KoxzBcjAmDjAPX3S_IMG_20260409_160404.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/trina77/images/KoxzBcjAmDjAPX3S_IMG_20260409_160404/KoxzBcjAmDjAPX3S_IMG_20260409_160404.webp)
给我们讲解的是个海归学者。他张口就说自己是项目4000万投入的受益者，这话一出，瞬间把大家的好奇心勾起来了——都想看看这4000万到底是怎么运作的。
 
他先讲办展初衷，说就是想让爱看书的孩子能写出自己的心里话，展厅里摆的都是各所小学孩子出的个人作品集。从2021年到2025年，这活动办了6届，他一直强调“特别成功”。展厅里那些孩子的刊物确实做得挺精致，看着挺有氛围。
 ![FH3C9jsf8HSm94NA_IMG_20260409_162940.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/trina77/images/FH3C9jsf8HSm94NA_IMG_20260409_162940/FH3C9jsf8HSm94NA_IMG_20260409_162940.webp)
其中这部作品《春姑娘》不仅书写成画还能创作成歌曲，对于孩子来说成就感满满。
![4JvToC55Eva2toH7_IMG_20260409_160410.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/trina77/images/4JvToC55Eva2toH7_IMG_20260409_160410/4JvToC55Eva2toH7_IMG_20260409_160410.webp)

![Fd6OdedJmT2WmiIt_IMG_20260409_160555.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/trina77/images/Fd6OdedJmT2WmiIt_IMG_20260409_160555/Fd6OdedJmT2WmiIt_IMG_20260409_160555.webp)
但咱这些天天扎在学校一线的人，心里都很清楚，这项目看着光鲜，实际根本不落地。
 
首先，每个学校都有自己的校本教材，阅读写作都有固定的安排，哪有多余精力去搞这种个人出刊、班刊的项目？
![02hMFlwIj90kkgij_IMG_20260409_163213.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/trina77/images/02hMFlwIj90kkgij_IMG_20260409_163213/02hMFlwIj90kkgij_IMG_20260409_163213.webp)
![wK1Dd1ohCiTqdRdE_IMG_20260409_163537.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/trina77/images/wK1Dd1ohCiTqdRdE_IMG_20260409_163537/wK1Dd1ohCiTqdRdE_IMG_20260409_163537.webp)
其次，能合作20个班以上的大学校本来就少，而且只有城区、县城的少数标杆校和民办校可能会感兴趣搞形象工程，普通学校、乡镇学校根本没这个需求和条件。
 ![BeEQ3BtT3McbaDUg_IMG_20260409_160713.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/trina77/images/BeEQ3BtT3McbaDUg_IMG_20260409_160713/BeEQ3BtT3McbaDUg_IMG_20260409_160713.webp)
说白了，这项目以学校为单位不切实际，就是脱离空想，完全没考虑到学校真实的教学和运营情况，想大范围推广，真的很难。说得再天花乱坠学校一句:没时间、没钱，我们就没辙了。

‎Hi Hive,
‎
‎I don’t have a lot of friends, if I’m being honest. But..
‎ https://img.leopedia.io/DQmNmxGjczjxoEx5wES3ratMo7wHUHRupVRwMrjyjohJBY9/IMG_20250904_160910_490.jpg 

‎I have lost quite a few friends over time, and now I can literally count the real ones in my life on one hand. It’s not like I have never had people around me. Though I have get to met many, laughed with many, and shared moments with many but when it comes to those who truly stayed and show up when matters  then I will say the number is small.
‎
‎And I have come to accept that.
‎
‎Een though I won’t sit here and act like I’m saint, perfect or that I wasn’t part of the reason why some friendships didn’t last long. I have changed and so is my mindset too. And most importantly, my standards for friendship and the type of people I want around me have changed too.
‎
‎People often say a good friend should be honest, loyal, kind and I agree because those are beautiful qualities of relationship after all. But it goes deeper than that for me even though I don’t really have a long list of requirements anymore.
‎
‎In fact, I have just one.
‎
‎Be there for me when I’m at my lowest. And that’s it.
‎
‎Because from my own experience, I’ve seen how people gather around you when things are going well, when you’re winning, smiling, and everything looks good on the outside, you’ll have company,  even a lots at that. But when the moment of life hits harder, the silence becomes louder.
‎
‎I’ve been there.
‎
‎I have had moments where I was at one of the lowest points in my life, and not even a single person I called a friend reached out to ask if I was okay or give a helping hand. Not even the person I was emotionally closest to at the time. That experience is what really changed me and made me understand that not everyone who laughs with you truly stands with you or happy about your existence.
‎
‎And since then, I have made a tough decision that I started letting people go especially those with bad and negative energy. Not out of anger, but out of clarity. Because I believe that anyone who  doesn't show up when you need them the most was never really there in the first place so I have to make that decision.
‎
‎Pease don’t get me wrong, I still value honesty, loyalty, and kindness but to me, the real test of friendship is presence and most especially during the hard and tough times.
‎
‎Because a true friend is not just someone who celebrates you but someone who sits with you when you’re broken and have nothing.
‎
‎So at this point in my life, I’m not looking for many friends but I'm just looking for real ones.
‎
‎
‎![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYaWnApEziAtLL5Zwv3ZNbDjRfSfG6h5njgTrpyasnE6y/1775569275821.png)

I am a very fussy gamer. I don't have a lot of patience for things that aren't what I am looking for in a game and I think that is perfectly ok. There are a ton of options for gamers and therefore I don't normally stick around for a game that doesn't fit the bill entirely for me. I quit on more games than I complete and I think that most people are that way. *Granblue Fantasy Relink* started out really great and I had a lot of good things to say about it in my previous writeup, but now I am going to focus on some of the things that turned me off about the game and also why I am unlikely to continue playing it. I have already moved on but want to point out the game's shortcomings just so people can have a good idea about the game in it's entirety.
https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/granbluefantasyrelinkendlessragnarok/16x9_GranblueFantasyRelinkEndlessRagnarok_image1600w.jpg [src](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/granbluefantasyrelinkendlessragnarok/16x9_GranblueFantasyRelinkEndlessRagnarok_image1600w.jpg)

CON: Combat takes too long

I think that the general idea here is that they were tying to make a game like the very popular *Monster Hunter* franchise that I tried to get into, but didn't really enjoy it. A lot of other people have though seeing as how they have sold something crazy like 100 million copies of those games. The issue I take with the central theme of the game being to defeat bosses on a regular basis is that these battles take a **Very long time**. Much of this has to do with the massive HP pool that said bosses have. The combat doesn't get any more difficult and honestly, the fights are actually pretty easy even once you step the game's difficulty up to "hard." I rarely step games up to hard level but I was breezing through bosses without really having any strategy at all.
https://images.microcms-assets.io/assets/eb99e2a508104ba88aaa382d1573ac14/ebf414f2b3c9494c845770e690e6e294/battles0010PS402.jpg [src](https://images.microcms-assets.io/assets/eb99e2a508104ba88aaa382d1573ac14/ebf414f2b3c9494c845770e690e6e294/battles0010PS402.jpg)
If you desire to do so, you can just stand really far back out of harm's way and let your 3 teammates do all the work. This will take longer but they will eventually win, even on hard. If you turn on the "assist" function the game basically plays itself. After a bunch of battles I found myself losing interest in even participating.

Con: Leveling up basically IS the story

I don't mind a game not having much in the way of a story, but as far as your objectives are concerned in this game, the entire point of all that you are doing seems to be leveling up all of your nearly 20 characters as well as their weapons in order to progress. The various things you can equip are very limited, and the only thing that you really need to do is occasionally visit the blacksmith and upgrade your main weapons.
https://www.siliconera.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/how-to-obtain-mastery-points-granblue-fantasy-relink.png [src](https://www.siliconera.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/how-to-obtain-mastery-points-granblue-fantasy-relink.png)
There is a massive "skill tree" that is called "Masteries" and while i put a bunch of time into choosing just the right things at first, I quickly came to the realization that none of this really makes that much of a difference and I believe the entire reasoning behind all of this is for this to be a time-sink so you will grind in order to level everyone up. While there is a main character in this game, you have the option of playing as anyone, which is kind of nice until all of your toons are many levels apart from one another and you are simply running around doing repetitive quests in order to get XP. I don't mind a bit of grinding, but after a bit that becomes the entire game and since combat kind of loses its lustre after a few hours, this stops being fun. I enjoy the casual nature of this game but after a bit you kind of get tired of simply hitting square all the time, hundreds of times in a row for a single battle.

Con: Too much voice acting

I think the voice acting in this game is actually done very well and I applaud that. I mentioned before that I think the way that you are able to skip nearly any scene or story segment is done very well in this game. However, there is constant yammering that takes place during fights that might have had good intentions but after a while I just want everyone to shut up because it adds nothing to the game and the talky talky talky is not relevant to what is actually going on in the battle itself (such as a companion warning you about incoming missiles or something like that).
https://images.microcms-assets.io/assets/eb99e2a508104ba88aaa382d1573ac14/b5dc4413c6c041d895b0f90cf4b38fe5/battles0090steam02.jpg [src](https://images.microcms-assets.io/assets/eb99e2a508104ba88aaa382d1573ac14/b5dc4413c6c041d895b0f90cf4b38fe5/battles0090steam02.jpg)
There also doesn't seem to be any rhyme or reason to why the various characters choose to talk. During the boss battles the amount of yammering is just a mess of characters talking over one another at the same time and it's annoying. I wish there was an option to disable this.

Con: Vyrn is irritating as hell

JRPG's seem to have some sort of intense fascination with some sort of cute floating character that follows the group around and give you hints about where to go and what to do.
https://images.rpgsite.net/image/da49c9a1/133294/original/Granblue-Fantasy-Relink_20240111_02.png [src](https://images.rpgsite.net/image/da49c9a1/133294/original/Granblue-Fantasy-Relink_20240111_02.png)
I have disliked this sort of character ever since *Zelda Ocarina of Time* introduced us to "Navi" all those years ago HEY! LISTEN! HEY LISTEN! I guess it is just protocol with Japanese-centric games but even though I have previously said the voice acting in this game is pretty dern good, Vyrn is just annoying in every sense. He/she/it is the Jar Jar Binks of this game and I hate that creature. When I looked into this a bit I found out that Japanese players have a similar disdain for this character when playing in Japanese.

Biggest CON for me, personally

The main reason why I am going to be stepping away from this game, probably permanently, is because many years ago MMORPG's kind of had some bad impacts on my real life and after that instance I decided that I wasn't going to play MMO's anymore. Now *Granblue Fantasy Relink* technically isn't an MMO but since the game never actually ends and your objective is to just play it forever like Diablo games or the Destiny series of sci-fi games. I prefer to play a game that has a beginning, a story, objectives, and finally an end. One of the commonly held scrutiny of *Granblue* is that the actual story part of the game is very short and the real objective of this game is "end game material" and that my friends, is something I have never enjoyed ever since writing off MMO's around a decade ago. *Granblue* is a pretty game that kind of lacks an identity. It isn't an MMO, it isn't a story adventure, it isn't a shooter, it's not really an open-world game either even though it tries to act like it is. For me, the cons outweigh the pros for this game and while such a game might appeal to other people, this one just isn't for me. If you do like casual RPG-like games that don't ever end and the whole idea is to just get more and more powerful and take on increasingly powerful boss fights, this might be a decent one for you to check out especially if you have a PS-Plus account because it is currently free and likely to stay that way for quite a while.
